subject: Request: one-time commercial credit for delayed model sharding feature
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeptuneAI — commercial ask for delayed sharding

Team — quick summary up front: NeptuneAI is asking for a one-time commercial accommodation (credit against Q3 consumption) because our model sharding capability that they committed their integration to will be pushed out by ~6 weeks. Sales has escalated on risk to their public launch and procurement is asking for numbers.

Key facts: 
- Account: NeptuneAI (Series B, ML infra-heavy customer)
- Contract: MSA + usage; signed; Q3 launch is tied to marketing commitments
- Technical gap: our model sharding (multi-GPU horizontal KV) optimization, which reduces latency/cost for their long-context workloads, will not be ready for their pilot window.

Request from Neptune: a timeboxed credit to offset expected incremental tokens/costs during pilot (estimated by them at ~15% of expected Q3 bill). Procurement asked us to propose a commercial number today.

Attachments: impact_modeling.xlsx (LAURA: included their request and our initial cost delta calc)

As product/eng owners, can you confirm:
1) realistic target to get a reduced-scope sharding release (hotfix path) vs full feature?
2) whether we have an alternate model variant (smaller sharded-friendly quant) we can offer as mitigation?
3) technical risk that would justify the commercial delta they requested?

I propose we craft an internal exec ask for a one-time commercial credit (not precedent-setting beyond this single pilot) and align on the precise $$ or % before I push to procurement. Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeptuneAI — commercial ask for delayed sharding

Laura — quick technical note:
- The primary blocker for the horizontal sharding GA is a combination of KV eviction correctness under high concurrency + a kernel scheduling path for cross-GPU attention. Both are close but require a week of focused engineering validation + a small safety rollout (canary lane).
- Reduced-scope hotfix: we can ship a restricted sharding mode that supports deterministic placement for static-length sessions in ~3 weeks (risk: less efficient for heterogeneous session lengths). This would satisfy many long-prompt customers, but Neptune's load profile includes highly variable sequence lengths — so it would help but not fully match their expectation.
- Alternate mitigation: we have a quantized single-GPU variant that reduces mem but increases token latency (approx +7% latency, cost neutral in some scenarios). That model is available to give them near-term relief.

I recommend we be transparent about the limited scope of the hotfix and price the commercial accommodation accordingly (not full 15% unless they demonstrate actual overage).

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeptuneAI — commercial ask for delayed sharding

Adding product context:
- Roadmap tradeoff: sharding GA was scoped for late Q2 but we diverted effort to some kernel-level safety fixes after a regression surfaced in internal canaries. We kept Neptune in the loop but did not lock the pilot SLA. My fault on communication slack — we should fix that process.
- Commercial ask framing: instead of an unconditional 15% credit, propose a usage-offset credit tied to observed token delta during the pilot (retrospective). That limits precedent risk and aligns incentives. Example: credit up to 12% of pilot invoice, phased — 6% up front conditional on pilot continuation, remainder after we verify telemetry.

I can own the rollout plan to give Neptune early access to the quantized model variant Marcus mentioned. If they accept that, their incremental delta will likely be <8% per our modeling. Grace — we will need a revops-approved credit template and guidance on authority levels.

Maya

--
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Product Management
maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Formal ask: one-time pilot credit (NeptuneAI) — request exec sign-off

Folks — thanks for the quick inputs. I drafted the formal commercial ask for Exec approval below. Please review and flag edits; I want to route this to Finance & Legal for signoff by EOD.

Summary (for execs):
- Ask: Approve a timeboxed, one-off commercial accommodation for NeptuneAI to cover increased inference cost caused by delayed model sharding.
- Proposal: Up to 12% credit on Neptune's pilot invoice, disbursed as follows: 6% as an up-front invoice credit (applied to first month), remaining up to 6% contingent on telemetry verification showing >4% measured delta vs our baseline. Cap the total credit at $85,000.
- Conditions:
  * Applies only to the NeptuneAI pilot tied to Deal DEAL-78912.
  * Customer must accept immediate access to the quantized model variant and permit telemetry sharing for 60 days.
  * This is a single-account, non-precedent concession approved as an exception.

Rationale:
- Protects a strategic early adopter whose public launch would materially increase platform credibility in the vector search space; avoids churn risk and preserves long-term ARR upside.
- Mitigates launch risk without altering core pricing policy; ties payout to measured impact.

Attachments and links: impact_modeling.xlsx (breakdown), HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/78912).

Requested approvals & owners: 
- RevOps / Grace O'Connor: confirm authority to grant up to $85k or suggest escalation path.
- Legal: confirm amendment language (I will draft).
- Finance: confirm accounting treatment and cash vs credit.

Grace — can you confirm today whether this sits within your approval limits? If so I will send an external amendment with the credit terms and the telemetry clause.

If not within your limit, please escalate to [Head of Revenue] and copy me. Laura — stand by to share the amendment with Sara at procurement once we have signoff.

Thanks — Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
